senses.en: a person between 13 and 19 years old
examples: Most **teenagers** in my class have a part-time hobby.
The club is for **teenagers** aged 14 to 18.
As a **teenager** he was very shy.

forms.en: aged between 13 and 19
forms.ex: She has two **teenage** sons.

teenager.note: The name comes from the numbers that end in *-teen*: thir**teen** to nine**teen**. Use the adjective *teenage* before a noun, not *teenager*: *a teenage boy*, never *a teenager boy*.

senses.en: the period of life when a child develops into an adult
senses.vi: tuổi dậy thì, giai đoạn vị thành niên
examples: **Adolescence** can be a confusing time.
Many changes happen during **adolescence**.
He was quiet throughout his **adolescence**.

forms.en: a young person going through this stage
forms.vi: thiếu niên; thuộc tuổi vị thành niên
forms.ex: **Adolescents** need plenty of sleep.

adolescence.note: Stress the third syllable: ad-o-**LES**-cence. More formal than *teenage years*.

senses.en: the strong feeling that you must do what people of your own age are doing in order to be accepted
senses.vi: áp lực từ bạn bè đồng trang lứa
examples: **Peer pressure** made him start smoking.
Learning to say no is the best answer to **peer pressure**.
She gave in to **peer pressure** and skipped the class.

forms.en: a person of the same age or position as you
forms.ex: He is respected by his **peers**.

senses.en: sure that you can do things well and that people will like you
examples: Speaking in class made her more **self-confident**.
He is **self-confident** enough to ask for help.
A **self-confident** student is not always the loudest one.

forms.en: belief in your own ability
forms.ex: Joining the club gave him **self-confidence**.

self-confident.note: Keep the hyphen. Compare *confident* (sure about something in general) with *self-confident* (sure about **yourself**).

senses.en: very pleased and happy
examples: I was **delighted** to hear your news.
She was **delighted** that her team had won.
My parents were **delighted** with my report.

delighted.note: Stronger than *pleased* or *glad*. Feelings adjective — the *-ed* form describes the **person**; the *-ing* form (*delightful*, *delighting*) describes the thing.

senses.en: feeling shy, awkward or ashamed, especially in front of other people
examples: I felt **embarrassed** when I forgot her name.
He was too **embarrassed** to sing in front of the class.
She looked **embarrassed** and went very red.

forms.en: making you feel embarrassed
forms.ex: It was an **embarrassing** mistake.

embarrassed.note: Two *r*s and two *s*s. The person is *embarrass**ed***; the situation is *embarrass**ing***.

senses.en: annoyed or impatient because you cannot do or change something
examples: I get **frustrated** when the internet is slow.
She was **frustrated** by her own mistakes.
He felt **frustrated** that nobody would listen.

forms.en: causing that feeling
forms.ex: Losing by one point was **frustrating**.

senses.en: worried and tense because of pressure from work, study or life
examples: Many students feel **stressed** before exams.
He gets **stressed** when he has too much homework.
You look **stressed** — take a break.

forms.en: worry caused by a difficult situation
forms.ex: Exercise helps reduce **stress**.

forms.en: causing stress
forms.ex: Exam week is **stressful**.

stressed.note: The person is *stress**ed***; the situation is *stress**ful***. In phonetics, *stress* also means the strong syllable in a word — the sense used in Units 9–12.

senses.en: wanting to know or learn about something
examples: Teenagers are naturally **curious** about the world.
I was **curious** to see what was inside.
She is **curious** about how things work.

senses.en: strange or unusual
examples: There was a **curious** smell in the room.
It is **curious** that nobody noticed.

forms.en: the wish to know about things
forms.ex: **Curiosity** is the best reason to read.

senses.en: to meet and spend time with other people in a friendly way
senses.vi: giao lưu, gặp gỡ mọi người
examples: Teenagers need time to **socialise** with their friends.
He doesn't **socialise** much during exam term.
Clubs are a good place to **socialise**.

socialise.note: British spelling *socialise*; American *socialize*. Do not confuse *social* (about meeting people) with *sociable* (a friendly person).

senses.en: a choice you make after finding out the facts you need
senses.vi: quyết định sáng suốt (dựa trên hiểu biết)
examples: Read about the course first so you can make an **informed decision**.
Teenagers should learn to make **informed decisions** about money.
It was an **informed decision**, not a guess.

forms.en: knowing about a subject because you have learned the facts
forms.vi: hiểu biết, nắm rõ thông tin
forms.ex: She is well **informed** about the issue.

senses.en: a practical ability you need in order to manage everyday life
examples: Cooking and managing money are useful **life skills**.
The school runs a **life skills** class on Fridays.
Saying no politely is an important **life skill**.

senses.en: the work of cleaning and looking after a house
examples: We all share the **housework** at home.
I do my **housework** before I go out.
He does more **housework** than anyone else in the family.

housework.note: **Uncountable** — never *houseworks* or *a housework*. Say *a lot of housework*. And you **do** housework; you don't *make* it. Not the same as *homework*, which is school work.

senses.en: to become a member of a group that meets for a shared activity
examples: Why don't you **join a club** and meet new people?
I **joined the** photography **club** last term.
She wants to **join a** chess **club** at school.

join a club.note: **Join** a club (become a member) is different from *join in* an activity (take part on one occasion).

senses.en: to start taking part in an activity or become connected with it
senses.vi: tham gia vào, dấn thân vào
examples: He **got involved in** a community project last year.
More students should **get involved in** school events.
Try not to **get involved in** their argument.

senses.en: to move or make progress at the same speed as someone or something else
examples: I can't **keep up with** the rest of the class in maths.
Walk slower — I can't **keep up with** you!
It's hard to **keep up with** all the homework.

senses.en: to continue to learn about something as it changes
senses.vi: cập nhật, theo dõi (tin tức, xu hướng)
examples: She **keeps up with** the news every morning.
It's impossible to **keep up with** every new app.

keep up with.note: Three parts, and they never separate: *keep up with **them***, never *keep them up with*.

senses.en: to take action in order to solve a problem or handle a situation
examples: How do you **deal with** stress before an exam?
The teacher **dealt with** the problem quickly.
I'll **deal with** it tomorrow morning.

senses.en: to be about a particular subject
examples: The article **deals with** teenage sleep.
Chapter three **deals with** the causes of the war.

senses.en: to spend time somewhere, or with someone, in a relaxed way with no particular plan
senses.vi: đi chơi, la cà, tụ tập
examples: We usually **hang out with** friends after school.
They **hang out** at the shopping centre on Saturdays.
I just want to **hang out** at home this weekend.

hang out (with).note: Informal. Use *with* for people and *at / in* for places. Irregular: hang → hung → hung.

senses.en: a place on the internet where a group of people leave messages for each other about a shared subject
examples: Our class has its own **forum** for homework questions.
She asked about the arts and crafts club on the school **forum**.
I read the **forum** every evening, but I rarely post anything.

forum.note: Plural *forums*. Messages go **on** a forum, not *in* one. In this unit it means an online message board, not a hall or a meeting.

senses.en: a school club whose members meet to practise a foreign language together
examples: The **language club** meets in Room 8 every Friday.
I joined the **language club** because I never speak English outside lessons.
Members of the **language club** share their own stories in English.

language club.note: Club names are built the same way: *chess club*, *sports club*, *music club*. The first noun says what happens there and stays **singular** — *a **book** club*, never *a books club*.

senses.en: making things by hand — drawing, painting, paper folding, simple woodwork and so on
examples: The **arts and crafts** club makes greeting cards for the school fair.
She spends Saturday mornings on **arts and crafts**.
Our **arts and crafts** teacher showed us how to fold a paper bird.

arts and crafts.note: A fixed phrase: both nouns stay plural and *and* never drops out. Before another noun it behaves as one adjective — *an **arts and crafts** lesson*.

senses.en: a club whose members meet to play or train at a sport together
examples: Our **sports club** trains twice a week after school.
The coach of the **sports club** used to play for the city team.
He joined a **sports club** to keep fit and to meet people.
colloc: the coach of the sports club

sports club.note: *Sport* keeps its **-s** inside this compound: *a **sports** club*, *a **sports** teacher*. On its own, British English says *I play **sport*** with no -s.

senses.en: to take part in an activity together with other people
examples: About forty students **participate in** the wellbeing club.
She **participates in** every competition the school runs.
I want to **participate in** two clubs this year, not four.

forms.en: the act of taking part
forms.ex: The teacher gives marks for **participation**, not only for tests.

participate (in).note: Always **in** before the activity. ⚠️ Compare with *join*, which takes the club straight after it: *I **joined** the club* but *I **participate in** the club*.

senses.en: unpaid work done to help the people who live in your area
senses.vi: hoạt động phục vụ cộng đồng
examples: The club does **community service** at the local library once a month.
**Community service** takes a whole Saturday, and none of us mind.
They repaired the benches in the park as **community service**.

community service.note: Uncountable: *some **community service***, never *a community service*. For one piece of it, say *a **community service** project*.

senses.en: working well together so that a group does better than its members would alone
senses.vi: sự làm việc nhóm, tinh thần đồng đội
examples: Cooking for thirty people takes real **teamwork**.
The club improved my **teamwork** far more than my drawing.
Good **teamwork** turned a slow job into a short one.

teamwork.note: One word and **uncountable** — *good **teamwork***, never *a teamwork* or *teamworks*. The people are *a **team***; what they do together is *teamwork*.

senses.en: one period of time spent doing a particular activity
examples: Each club **session** lasts forty minutes.
We held an extra practice **session** before the competition.
I missed one **session** and fell behind everybody else.

session.note: A *session* is **one** meeting. The whole series of them is a *course*, a *club* or a *term*.

senses.en: pleasant, so that you are glad you did it
senses.vi: thú vị, dễ chịu, đáng thích
examples: The first club meeting was surprisingly **enjoyable**.
She makes even grammar **enjoyable**.
It was an **enjoyable** afternoon, and nobody wanted to go home.

forms.en: to get pleasure from something
forms.ex: I **enjoy** cooking at the weekend.

enjoyable.note: **Things** are enjoyable; **people** are pleased or happy. ❌ *I was enjoyable.* ✅ *I **enjoyed** it.* The /ɔɪ/ of *enjoy* stays in *enjoyable*.

senses.en: the websites and apps where people post messages, pictures and videos for other people to see
examples: Most of my classmates use **social media** every day.
**Social media** is the fastest way to tell everyone about the club.
He stayed off **social media** for a month during the midterm tests.

forms.en: the ways news and messages reach large numbers of people
forms.ex: The **media** reported the flood within an hour.

social media.note: Treated as **uncountable** in everyday English: *social media **is** …*. Never *a social media* — say *a **social media** site* or *an app*. (*Media* began as the plural of *medium*, so formal writing sometimes keeps *the media **are** …*.)

senses.en: to move a file from your own device onto the internet so that other people can see it
examples: He **uploaded** the club photos the same evening.
I can't **upload** the video — the file is too big.
She **uploads** a new drawing every Sunday.

forms.en: to move a file from the internet onto your own device
forms.ex: I **downloaded** the club timetable to my phone.

upload.note: *Up* = away from your device, out to the internet; *down* = the other way. ⚠️ What follows is the **file you send**: *upload **a picture***, never *upload **the website***.

senses.en: a short message from an app or a site telling you that something new has happened
examples: My phone shows twenty **notifications** every morning.
She checks her **notifications** between lessons.
Turn your **notifications** off while you are revising.

forms.en: to tell someone officially about something
forms.ex: The club will **notify** members by email.

notification.note: The usual verb is **check**: *I **check** my notifications*. Countable, so it takes the plural **-s** — and in practice it is nearly always plural.

senses.en: to type your name and password so that you can start using a computer system or an account
examples: I **log on to** my account every evening.
She **logged on** and found nine new messages waiting.
You have to **log on** before you can post on the forum.

forms.en: to stop using an account and close it safely
forms.ex: Always **log out** on a school computer.

log on (to).note: Name the account or the site and you need **to**: *log on **to** your account*. With nothing after it, plain *log on*. ⚠️ Never *log on your account*.

senses.en: an arrangement that lets you use a website or an app, with your own name and password
examples: She opened an **account** on the photo app last week.
Keep your **account** password to yourself.
He has two **accounts** — one for his family and one for the club.

account.note: You **open** or **create** an account; you do not *make* one. The money kind is *a **bank** account* — same word, different world.

senses.en: a set of pages on the internet kept in one place by a person, a school or a company
examples: The school **website** lists every club and its meeting day.
I browsed three **websites** before I found the right form.
Their **website** is slow, but the information on it is good.

website.note: One word. Things sit **on** a website: *the timetable is **on** the school website*. One page is a *web page*; the whole set is a *website*.

senses.en: easy to use, even the first time you try it
senses.vi: dễ dùng, thân thiện với người dùng
examples: The new club app is **user-friendly**, so nobody needed help.
A **user-friendly** site does not make you read instructions first.
She chose that one because it was the most **user-friendly** of the three.

user-friendly.note: Keep the hyphen. The pattern *noun + -friendly* means 'easy or kind for that thing': *child-friendly*, *eco-friendly*.

senses.en: to get in touch with people, or stay in touch with them, especially online
examples: I **connect with** my cousins in Hue almost every day.
The forum lets us **connect with** students in the other classes.
She **connected with** three friends from her old primary school.

senses.en: to join one thing to another
examples: This cable **connects** the camera to the computer.
A short path **connects** the two school buildings.

forms.en: a link between two people or two things
forms.vi: sự kết nối, mối liên hệ
forms.ex: The **connection** dropped in the middle of the call.

connect (with).note: People take **with**, machines and places take **to**. ⚠️ *connect **with** friends*, not *connect friends*.

senses.en: happening in the middle of a school term
examples: Our **midterm** tests start on Monday.
She was calm before the **midterm** exam and surprised afterwards.
**Midterm** week is the most stressful week of the year.

midterm.note: Used **before** a noun: *a **midterm** test*. British English also writes it *mid-term*. The one at the end of the term is the *final* test.

senses.en: what someone believes you will do, or should be able to do
examples: My parents have high **expectations**, and that is hard on a bad week.
He met every **expectation** his teachers had of him.
Her only **expectation** was that we would try.

forms.en: to believe that something will happen
forms.ex: They **expect** me to come first in every subject.

expectation.note: Expectations **of** a person (what you want from them), but expectations **for** a year or a term. ⚠️ You **meet** expectations — you do not *reach* them.

senses.en: to give all your attention to one thing
examples: I can't **concentrate** when my phone keeps buzzing.
Chess taught him to **concentrate on** one problem at a time.
She **concentrated** so hard that she forgot the time.

forms.en: the ability to give something your full attention
forms.ex: Forty minutes is a long time for full **concentration**.

concentrate (on).note: The thing you attend to follows **on**: *concentrate **on** the lesson*. ⚠️ Never *concentrate to* or *concentrate in*.

senses.en: giving your full attention to what you are doing
examples: He has been much more **focused** since he joined the chess club.
A **focused** half-hour beats a whole distracted evening.
She stays **focused** even when the room is noisy.

forms.en: to give your attention to one thing; that attention
forms.ex: Try to **focus** on one subject at a time.

focused.note: One **-s-** in every form: *focus → focused → focusing*. Use the adjective for the person — *he is **focused*** — and the verb *concentrate* for the action: *he **concentrates** well*.

senses.en: behaving sensibly and thinking of other people, the way an adult is expected to
examples: She is very **mature** for fourteen.
Saying sorry first is the **mature** thing to do.
He became more **mature** after a year of looking after his brother.

forms.en: sensible adult behaviour
forms.ex: He handled the argument with surprising **maturity**.

mature.note: The stressed vowel is /ʊə/ — ma-**TURE**, the same sound as *tourist*. The opposite is *immature*.

senses.en: someone who frightens or hurts a weaker person again and again
examples: A **bully** never picks on someone their own size.
The **bully** in that story is lonelier than anyone else in it.
Tell a teacher if a **bully** is making school miserable.

senses.en: to frighten or hurt a weaker person again and again
examples: Nobody should be **bullied** for the way they look.
He **bullied** younger students until the school stepped in.

forms.en: the behaviour of a bully
forms.ex: The school has clear rules about **bullying**.

bully.note: Watch the vowel: /ˈbʊli/, the short sound of *book* — not /ˈbʌli/. Plural *bullies*; past tense *bullied*.
